The test image shows a corn ear with the husk peeled back, revealing large, fleshy, white-to-gray galls replacing the kernels. This is a classic presentation of **Common_smut** — the galls are young (still white/gray/fleshy, before the teliospores turn black). The reference collage confirms this exact appearance: fleshy, lumpy, pale galls on the ear, matching both the lower-right panel (green/white fleshy galls) and the overall ear gall morphology.

Key distinguishing features:
- Large fleshy galls replacing kernels on the ear
- White to gray color (early stage, not yet turned black)
- Galls clearly visible inside the husk
- Not Head_smut (which would show teardrop-shaped ears with threadlike vascular bundles and black spore masses)
